simple.meaning: נָקַף (nâqaph) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to strike with more or less violence ( beat , fell , corrode ); by implication (of attack) to knock together , i.e. surround or circulate.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 19 times across Leviticus, Joshua, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, and 4 more, beginning at Leviticus 19:27. Its contexts include kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָקַף (H5362).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָקַף (nâqaph) / H5362 is traced through Leviticus 19:27, Joshua 6:3, Joshua 6:11, 1 Kings 7:24 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5362. naqaph I. [ נָקַף ] verb strike off (Late Hebrew strike, wound , Aramaic נְקַף id. ; Arabic fregit caput, ut cerebrum appareret; Vulgar Arabic snap with the finger (Dozy ii. 716 ); Assyrian na‡pu probably= mutilated ; Ethiopic peel, flay Di 649 ); — Niph`al Perfect 3masculine singular הַיַּ֫עַר סִבְכֵי וְנִקַּף consecutive Isa 10:34 and the thickets of the forest shall be struck away (on singular verb compare Ges § 145o Da Synt. § 113 b ; or. read נִקְּפוּ ; — form possibly Pi`el, but compare Di Du Che Hpt ). Pi`el Perfect 3plural נִקְּפוּזֹֿאת עוֺרִי וְאַחַר Job 19:25 after my skin, which they (Ges § 144g ) have struck off (alluding to ravages of his disease) — this! but text dubious; Bu נִקַּף כָּזאֹת Niph`al which has been thus struck off. II. [ נָקַף verb ] go around (intransitive), (Ecclus 45:9 Hiph`il ויקיפהו surround something with (2 accusative); Perfect 3 feminine singular הקיפה 43:12 (accusative+ ב instrumental); Late Hebrew Hiph`il הִקִּיף = Biblical Hebrew; also = cling to, be attached, joined to , and so Aramaic אַקֵּיף (Aph`el), ); Qal Imperfect יִנְקֹ֑פוּ חַגִּים Isa 29:1 (figurative) let feasts go around , i.e. run the round (of the year). Hiph`il Perfect הִקִּיף Job 19:6 ; 3 feminine singular הִקִּ֫יפָהִ Isa 15:8 ; 3 plural הִקִּ֫יפוּ Job 1:5 ; Psa 88:18 , וְהִקִּיפוּ consecutive 2Chr 23:7 , suffix הִקִּיפוּנִי Psa 22:17 ; 2 masculine plural וְהִקַּפְתֶּם consecutive 2Kin 11:8 ; Imperfect וַיַּקַּף Lam 3:5 ; 3 masculine plural יַקִּ֫יפוּ Psa 17:9 , וַיַּקִּ֫פוּ 2Kin 6:14 ; 2 masculine plural תַּקִּ֫פוּ Lev 19:27 ; Imperative masculine plural suffix הַקִּיפ֫וּהָ Psa 48:13 ; Infinitive absolute הַקֵּיף Josh 6:3 , הַקֵּף 6:11 ; Participle plural מַקִּ(י)פִים 1Kin 7:24 ; 2Chr 4:3 ; — 1 go around, surround, encompass: a. go around , with accusative of city, Josh 6:3 compare 6:11 (accusative omitted), Psa 48:13 (all || סָבָב ); also (figurative) אֶתֿ הַזְּעָקָה הִקִּ֫יפָה Isa 15:8 the cry hath gone about the border of Moab. b. surround, encompass, enclose , usually with עַלהָֿעִיר וַיַּקִּ֫פוּ ׃עַלֿ 2Kin 6:14 and they closed in upon the city (beleaguered it); with עַל person 11:8 (+ סָבִיב ), Psa 17:9 ; 88:18 (|| סָבַב ), + accusative of thing Job 19:6 he hath closed his net in upon me compare Lam 3:5 ; less often with accusative of person Psa 22:17 (|| סָבַב ), 2Chr 23:7 (|| 2Kin 11:8 ; + סָבִיב ), also of inanimate things 1Kin 7:24 2Chr 4:3 (both + סָבִיב , || סָבַב ). 2 make the round , i.e. complete the circuit ׳הִקּ הַמִּשְׁתֶּה יְמֵי Job 1:5 when the days of feasting had completed their circuit . 3 make round, round off (literally): חַקּ ׳לֹא ראֹשְׁכֶם מְּאַת Lev 19:27 (|| זְקָנֶ֑ךָ מְּאַת אֵת תַשְׁחִית לֹא ), of heathen rite. קוף (√of following; apparently = II. נקף , go around ).

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘You shall not cut the hair on the sides of your head or clip off the edge of your beard.
All of your men of war shall march around the city, going around the city once. You shall do this six days.
So he caused Yahweh’s ark to go around the city, circling it once. Then they came into the camp, and stayed in the camp.
Under its brim around there were buds which encircled it for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The buds were in two rows, cast when it was cast.
Therefore he sent horses, chariots, and a great army there. They came by night, and surrounded the city.
You shall surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand; and he who comes within the ranks, let him be slain. Be with the king when he goes out, and when he comes in.”
Under it was the likeness of oxen, which encircled it, for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast when it was cast.
The Levites shall surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand. Whoever comes into the house, let him be slain. Be with the king when he comes in, and when he goes out.”

It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.
know now that God has subverted me,
from the wicked who oppress me,
I can count all of my bones.
You have put lover and friend far from me,
He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.
For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab, its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.
Woe to Ariel! Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year; let the feasts come around;
